unit.title: Verb Tenses and a Day in Your Life

contentBlocks.text: ਪਿਛਲੇ ਹਫ਼ਤੇ ਤੁਸੀਂ ਰਸਮੀ ਚਿੱਠੀ ਲਿਖਣਾ ਸਿੱਖਿਆ। ਇਸ ਹਫ਼ਤੇ: ਵਿਆਕਰਣ ਵਿੱਚ ਮੁਹਾਰਤ, ਕਾਲ ਤੋਂ ਸ਼ੁਰੂ! (Last week you learned formal letter writing. This week: grammar mastery, starting with tense!)

So far you've mostly used present tense (ਖੇਡਦਾ ਹਾਂ, 'I play'). Past tense shows something already happened: ਖਾਧਾ/ਖਾਧੀ means 'ate,' and ਗਿਆ/ਗਈ means 'went' — remember these change with gender, just like verbs always have. Practice: say 'ਮੈਂ ਸਕੂਲ ਗਿਆ' (I went to school, for a boy) or 'ਮੈਂ ਸਕੂਲ ਗਈ' (for a girl).
ਤੁਸੀਂ ਭੂਤਕਾਲ ਸਿੱਖਿਆ! (You just learned past tense!) Tomorrow we'll learn future tense.

objectives: Learn past-tense forms ਖਾਧਾ/ਖਾਧੀ (ate) and ਗਿਆ/ਗਈ (went)
Use ਗਿਆ/ਗਈ correctly with matching gender in a self-referential sentence
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review last week's formal-letter-writing content briefly.
2. Introduce past tense, contrasting with the present tense used so far.
3. Have the child say 'ਮੈਂ ਸਕੂਲ ਗਿਆ/ਗਈ' about themselves.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's future-tense lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just ਗਿਆ/ਗਈ first, the more immediately useful of the two past-tense verbs
Ready for more: ask the child to say a full sentence about something they actually did yesterday, using past tense
This opens the course's 'grammar mastery' thread with a genuinely new grammatical concept (tense) beyond earlier grades' present-tense-only sentences
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a vocabulary-acquisition activity — check that the child correctly traces/writes both past-tense verb pairs and uses ਗਿਆ/ਗਈ with the correct gender for themselves.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses the course's 'grammar mastery' goal, introducing tense as a genuinely new grammatical concept.

generationData.instructions: Trace each word, then copy it once on your own.
